title: regional-silo-and-gpu-pool-degradation-injector
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Validate end-to-end behavior when a region becomes isolated combined with progressive GPU pool exhaustion and dependent-service blackholes. We will test that: (1) smart routing and regional failover correctly evacuate traffic according to configured policies; (2) circuit breakers and admission controls prevent cascading failures and protect higher-priority tenants; (3) load-shedding triggers graceful degradation with clear error modes; (4) observed SLOs (availability and p99 latency) and error-budget accounting reflect expected impact and rollback thresholds.

Scope: Synthetic multi-tenant workload driven from two injected origins (internal traffic generator in us-east-1 and us-west-2). Faults injected include: a) network partition for a single region (simulated control-plane ejection + host-level blackholes), b) staged GPU pool drain (gradual worker process SIGSTOP/CPU cap/VM live drain to reduce GPU capacity by 25%/50%/75%), c) dependent-service blackholes (RPC timeouts and 503 responses from model-store/caching layer), and d) inter-region link flakiness (latency spikes and packet loss).

Acceptance criteria:
- Canary tenants failover within configured target (<= 45s to first success response in target region for warm KV-cached requests).
- For non-cached short requests, p99 latency stays within 2x baseline or triggers documented load-shedding path with clear 429 or 503 semantics.
- No customer data is routed to the wrong geographic tenant (data residency guardrails verified).
- Circuit breaker trips for unhealthy dependencies within configured thresholds and triggers automatic retry-backoff policies.
- Observation and dashboards capture SLO burn rate and provide actionable diffs (latency histogram, error taxonomy, token-level cost delta).

Test plan and tooling:
- Use chaos-harness v2 (github.com/redwood-inference/chaos-harness) to orchestrate region partition and host-level faults; PR: #1189.
- Extend load-generator (locust-derived) to mix short chat completions (16–64 tokens), mid-length completions (512 tokens), and long-context inference (4k tokens) to exercise KV cache behavior and backend batching.
- Implement a staged GPU drain controller that signals node pools to gracefully quiesce clients and then simulates sudden eviction.
- Dependency proxy shim to inject latencies and 503/connection-reset behavior for model-store and caching tiers.
- Runbook: defined rollback triggers (error budget burn > 25% in 5m window OR cross-tenant high-priority SLA breach) with automated rollback to route-only-to-hosted-fallback-model and capacity-scaling actions.

Observability and telemetry to collect:
- Per-tenant p50/p95/p99 latency and success rates, grouped by region and model-variant.
- Admission control / circuit-breaker state transitions with timestamps.
- GPU pool utilization, queue length, eviction counts, and kernel-level OOM/warning logs.
- Control-plane decision traces (why a request routed/fallbacked) and sample request traces for debugging.

Security / compliance notes:
- No customer PII will be used in synthetic traces. Test infra uses anonymized tenant IDs with residence tags preserved.
- Ensure KMS/HSM keys are not exposed by the test harness; make a read-only snapshots of audit logs only.

Next steps:
- Finalize chaos playbook and run in staging on 2025-03-06.
- Coordinate with on-call, SRE rotation, and platform PM to authorize a scheduled window.
- Land PR #1189 and the GPU drain controller (PR #1214) before run.
